Walkthrough

The change adds Redis pending-session tracking and periodic sweeps to recover missed wakes. It also changes held-open polling to respond to wake state and adds retry state for failed delivery-table writes. **Changes: SSE Wake and Delivery Recovery** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Pending-session queue tracking**
`src/Domain/Contract/SseSessionQueueInterface.php`, `src/Application/Service/Async/SseRedisSessionQueue.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/Fixture/CountingSessionQueue.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/SseRedisSessionQueueTest.php`|The queue contract and Redis implementation add pending-session reads and clearing. Queue writes mark session IDs in expiring time buckets before publishing wakes. Tests cover bucket reads, clearing, and Redis command failures.| |**Sweep and wake orchestration**
`src/Application/Service/Async/SseSessionRegistry.php`, `src/Application/Service/Async/SsePendingSweep.php`, `src/Application/Service/Async/SseWakeSubscriber.php`, `src/Application/Service/Async/SseServer.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/SsePendingSweepTest.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/SseSessionRegistryTest.php`|The registry tracks delivery-table wakes. The sweep reads pending IDs and wakes open held sessions, and the healthy subscriber timer runs it when due. Server wiring passes the sweep to the subscriber.| |**Held-open polling and delivery retries**
`src/Application/Service/Async/SseHeldOpenState.php`, `src/Application/Service/Async/SseServer.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/SseHeldOpenStateTest.php`, `tests/Unit/Async/HeldOpenLoopIdleRedisTest.php`|The held-open loop removes the five-second Redis safety poll and drains the delivery table when wake or retry state requires it. Failed frame writes remain available for a later attempt. Tests cover polling deadlines, idle scans, missed wakes, and refused writes.| **Estimated code review effort:** 3 (Moderate) | ~25 minutes **Change:** Refactor ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant SseRedisSessionQueue participant Redis participant SseWakeSubscriber participant SsePendingSweep participant SseSessionRegistry SseRedisSessionQueue->>Redis: Add session ID to pending bucket SseWakeSubscriber->>SsePendingSweep: Run sweep when due and healthy SsePendingSweep->>Redis: Read current and preceding pending buckets Redis-->>SsePendingSweep: Return pending session IDs SsePendingSweep->>SseSessionRegistry: Wake open held sessions SsePendingSweep->>Redis: Clear locally owned pending IDs ``` **Possibly related PRs** - [semitexa/semitexa-ssr#190](https://github.com/semitexa/semitexa-ssr/pull/190): Introduces the Redis wake path and subscriber that this change extends with pending-session sweeps.
Merge Risk: Low · up to b2dbe

A replaced SSE connection can take up to one heartbeat interval longer to stand down if its takeover wake is missed and the replacement worker sweeps first. The effect is small and self-recovering, so the change looks mergeable with owner awareness.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: an idle SSE stream no longer runs its own Redis safety poll, and one pending-set sweep per worker replaces it. The raw summary confirms the removal of the five-second per-stream poll and the addition of SsePendingSweep, which runs on a timer and wakes held sessions from the pending set. The title is specific and matches the stated objective of reducing idle-stream CPU use.
